chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Hammad ibn Isa from Ibrahim ibn Umar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding
a man who had sexual intercourse with a young boy (or eunuch), is his mother permissible to him? He said, 'If he was pierced in him, then no.'
The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: 'Whoever accuses his wife of adultery while she is mute or deaf, they are separated, and she is not permissible to him forever.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man marrying his mother if he has intercourse with a young boy or eunuch?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific condition of 'thaqaba' (penetration) required for establishing 'lawn' (consanguinity by marriage) when a man has intercourse with a young boy or eunuch, thereby determining if his mother becomes permanently prohibited to him. Shaykh al-Tusi extends this logic to 'khulw' (permanent separation due to false accusation of adultery), noting that if a man accuses his mute or deaf wife of zina, they are permanently separated and she does not become permissible to him again, mirroring the permanence of the marital bond in the primary case.
